speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any other neurological symptoms such as weakness, numbness, or vision changes? Additionally, how long have these balance issues been present?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; the "drunk" appearance and clumsiness on the right side are concerning for cerebellar involvement. To narrow this down, have you noticed any slurred speech, double vision, or involuntary eye movements? Also, have you had any recent severe headaches, falls, or a new tremor?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a critical piece of information; given your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab, we must urgently rule out Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_Review.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Findings show lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images reveal multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease. The MRI findings of non-enhancing multifocal demyelinating lesions in the absence of gadolinium enhancement are classic for this opportunistic infection. Given the confirmed diagnosis, I must immediately advise stopping natalizumab and initiating a consultation with Infectious Disease for potential immunomodulatory therapies and monitoring for JC virus reactivation.
